summary: Edward Delavan Perry was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He earned his A.B. at Columbia University (~1871-1875) and his Dr. phil. at the University of Tübingen (~1877-1879), later serving as Jay Professor of Greek and Latin at Columbia (1891-1931).

Edward Denison Ross worked in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Marlborough College, University College London, and under Theodor Nöldeke at the University of Strasbourg (Dr. phil.). He held posts at UCL, Aliah University, and SOAS (1916-1937).

Edward Elbridge Salisbury was an Indology and linguistics scholar. Educated at Yale (1828-1832) and under Woolsey, de Sacy, de Tassy, Bopp, Burnouf, and Lassen, he served as professor of Arabic and Sanskrit at Yale (1841-1854) and president of the American Oriental Society.

Edward Evan Evans-Pritchard was a religious studies scholar. He studied at Exeter College, Oxford (~1921-1924) and the London School of Economics (~1924-1927). He held academic posts at the LSE, Cairo University, Cambridge, and served as a professor at Oxford (1946-1970).

Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle is a scholar in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He completed his doctoral studies under Roderick S. Bucknell (attested 1994) and held a post at the University of Sydney.

Edward Garrett is a linguist and Tibetologist. He earned his Ph.D. at UCLA (~1996-2001) under Carson T. Schütze and Dominique Sportiche, and was mentored by Anna Szabolcsi. He worked as a research assistant at UCLA and the University of Virginia.

Edward Granville Browne specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and history/archaeology. Educated at Cambridge and St Bartholomew's under William Wright and Edward Byles Cowell, he served at Cambridge as lecturer in Persian (1888) and Adams Professor of Arabic (1902).

Edward H. Schafer was a sinologist who studied at UCLA, UC Berkeley (B.A.), the University of Hawaiʻi (M.A.), and Harvard (Ph.D.). He spent his career at UC Berkeley (~1947-1984) and served as president of the American Oriental Society (1975-1976).

Edward Hamilton Johnston was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. After studying at Eton College and New College, Oxford, he served in the Indian Civil Service (~1909-1927) and later as a professor at the University of Oxford (~1937-1942).

Edward James Rapson was a scholar of Indology, history/archaeology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. Educated at St John's College, Cambridge, he served at the British Museum (1887-1906), University College London (1903), and as Professor of Sanskrit at Cambridge (1906-1936).

Edward Joseph Thomas was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under John Burnet at the University of St Andrews and attended Cambridge. He served at Cambridge University Library (~1909-1935) and as Dean of the Oriental Languages Department at Cambridge (1946).

Edward Kamens is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Yale University (~1970-1982) and had a long career there (~1986-2020), becoming Sumitomo Professor Emeritus of East Asian Languages & Literatures around 2020.

Edward Moore is a researcher in computational fields and history/archaeology. As of 2026, he is attested as a PhD student and Associate Lecturer at Lancaster University studying under doctoral supervisor Patricia Murrieta-Flores.

Edward S. Casey is a philosopher who studied at Yale, Sorbonne under Paul Ricœur, and Northwestern (Ph.D.). He taught at UCSB, Yale, and Stony Brook University (~1978), and served as president of the American Philosophical Association (2009-2010).

Edward Sapir was a linguist who studied at Columbia University under Wilhelm Wundt and Franz Boas. He served at the Geological Survey of Canada (~1910-1925), the University of Chicago (~1925-1931), and Yale University (~1931-1939).

Edward Upham was a scholar in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He was a member of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland (~1824-1834) and a fellow of the Society of Antiquaries of London (~1832-1834).

Edward Vernon Arnold was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the University of Cambridge and at the University of Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth. He was a fellow at Trinity College, Cambridge, and professor at Bangor University (1884-1924).

Edward W. Said studied at Princeton University (~1953-1957) and Harvard University (~1957-1964). He held a long-standing academic post in English and Comparative Literature at Columbia University from around 1963 to 2003.

Edward Washburn Hopkins was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Columbia and under Albrecht Weber and Ernst Windisch at Leipzig (Ph.D.). He taught at Columbia, Bryn Mawr College, and served as professor at Yale University (1895-1926).

Edward Winslow Bastian is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, studied with several traditional Geshes, and was a research scholar at Banaras Hindu University.
